=== STEP-2 DOCS-TRUTH VERIFIED (2026-06-08) ===
• [trino.io/docs/467/sql/select.html](https://trino.io/docs/467/sql/select.html) — Trino 467 SELECT grammar (WebFetch result, exact synopsis quoted): `[ WITH FUNCTION sql_routines ] [ WITH [ RECURSIVE ] with_query [, ...] ] SELECT [ ALL | DISTINCT ] select_expression [, ...] [ FROM from_item [, ...] ] [ WHERE condition ] [ GROUP BY [ ALL | DISTINCT ] grouping_element [, ...] ] [ HAVING condition] [ WINDOW window_definition_list] [ { UNION | INTERSECT | EXCEPT } [ ALL | DISTINCT ] select ] [ ORDER BY expression [ ASC | DESC ] [, ...] ] [ OFFSET count [ ROW | ROWS ] ] [ LIMIT { count | ALL } ]`. **QUALIFY is ABSENT from the documented clause list.** Confirms `... QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...) = 1` is a PARSE ERROR (`mismatched input 'QUALIFY'`) in Trino 467, with no graceful degradation.
• [trinodb/trino #20687](https://github.com/trinodb/trino/issues/20687) — QUALIFY is tracked as an OPEN feature request not yet implemented (cross-ref already at r27:3784).
• [trino.io/docs/467/functions/aggregate.html](https://trino.io/docs/467/functions/aggregate.html) — `max_by(x, y) -> [same as x]`: 'Returns the value of x associated with the maximum value of y over all input values.' `min_by(x, y) -> [same as x]` symmetric. 3-arg forms return `array<[same as x]>` for top/bottom-N. Both VERIFIED.
• Run-directive form 1 (preferred — first/last/min/max-by-a-key, one row per group, no window, no dedup): `min_by(x, sort_key)` / `max_by(x, sort_key)` GROUP BY entity. e.g. latest status per device: `SELECT device_id, max_by(status, reading_time) AS latest_status, MAX(reading_time) AS latest_time FROM device_readings GROUP BY device_id`. e.g. first AND last amount per customer one row (Q2 shape): `SELECT customer_id, min_by(amount, order_date) AS first_amount, max_by(amount, order_date) AS last_amount FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id`. VERIFIED against docs.
• Run-directive form 2 (general top-N-per-group — whole rows or N>1): wrap window in subquery / CTE then filter `WHERE rn <= N` outside. `SELECT * FROM (SELECT t.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY k DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM t) WHERE rn = 1`. VERIFIED against the existing §3.1G canonical SQL block at r23:999-1010.
